html:
"Principality of Novgorod" is the map's label, for 1200, for the lands of Novgorod, the great trading city of northern Rus, which by then was a republic; see Novgorod Republic.

In 1136 the people of Novgorod drove out their prince and from then on chose their own. A town assembly, the veche, and elected officials ran the city, along with the archbishop and rich boyar families. Novgorod's lands stretched north to the White Sea and east to the Urals, and its merchants sold furs, wax and walrus ivory to the Hanseatic traders. Ordinary townspeople wrote letters on birch bark, and hundreds have been dug up.

Novgorod escaped the Mongol sack, and its prince Alexander Nevsky beat the Swedes in 1240 and the German knights in 1242. It also ruled the Karelians. In 1478 Ivan III of Moscow annexed it. The later map label is Novgorod.
